correctness.rationale: For 0<p<q<=infty every rank-r nonzero matrix satisfies ||A||_q/||A||_p >=r^(1/q−1/p), including quasi-norm p<1, exponent negative. The penultimate codimension condition forces a real 2-plane. For even N, span(I,J) with J real skew-orthogonal has all N singular values sqrt(a²+b²), saturating the universal bound. For odd N the determinant of a real odd-degree pencil changes sign under (a,b)↦−(a,b), forcing a nonzero rank<=N−1 member on every 2-plane; embedding an N−1 even conformal block saturates that bound. A scalar line gives last c_(N²). Independent exact integer Gram checks N=2..15 corroborate but proof works for all N>=2 and all given exponents.
residual_risks: Numerical/finite Gram examples prove neither every matrix-pencil obstruction nor full parameter quantification.

originality.rationale: Prochno 2026 Theorem A and Remark 1.1 give broad all-index asymptotic bounds and the exact last c_(N²), but not this parity-sensitive penultimate index. Earlier Hinrichs–Prochno–Vybíral and Prochno–Strzelecki estimates similarly lack this exact last-two comparison. A published two-row rectangular theorem and complex 3×3 result cannot directly specialize to square N×N for all N. Standard real skew-complex structures and odd pencil singularity are credited ingredients; a classical matrix-pencil widths corollary remains a priority risk.
